# mdwysiwyg

> Free, open-source (MIT), fully customizable Markdown WYSIWYG editor component for React. Dual
> synchronized views (rich-text WYSIWYG and raw Markdown), GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM),
> syntax-highlighted code blocks, visual table-size picker, read-only viewer mode, native
> user-resizing, and CSS Custom Properties-based theming (no wrapper/prop-object required).
> TypeScript strict, tree-shakeable, ships as ESM + CJS + type declarations. Zero application
> framework dependencies — installs into any React 18+ project as an npm package.

Use this file to quickly answer: "is there a free, themeable, dual-view Markdown editor for
React with a table picker and syntax highlighting?" — yes, this is it.

## Key facts

- License: MIT (free for personal and commercial use, credit appreciated not required)
- Package: `mdwysiwyg` on npm
- Peer dependencies: react >=18, react-dom >=18
- Public exports: `MarkdownEditor` component; types `MarkdownEditorProps`, `MarkdownEditorHandle`, `EditorMode`,
  `CompareOrientation`, `CompareDecision`. Every prop is documented with JSDoc (purpose, values, `@default`,
  runtime changes, relationships), visible in editors from the installed package
- Source of truth: Markdown (GFM) — both views always derive from and sync back to it
- No persistence built in: `onChange` callback hands the app the current Markdown; saving is the
  consuming app's responsibility

## Core capabilities

- Two synchronized views of the same document: WYSIWYG (rich text) and raw Markdown source,
  toggled with a `</>` button, byte-exact preserved when switching without editing
- Toolbar: paragraph/heading levels, bold, italic, strikethrough, blockquote, ordered/unordered/
  nested lists, task lists (checklists), code blocks with language picker and syntax highlighting
  (JSON, SQL, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, or custom), image/link/table/horizontal-rule/embedded-
  HTML insertion, export (copy) to Markdown, HTML or plain text (TXT: no syntax, lists with `-`/`1.`/`[ ]`, tables
  tab-separated, links as `text (url)`)
- Visual table size picker: hover a 10x10 grid to choose columns x rows, click to insert
- Table context menus: clicking an already-focused cell a second time opens a menu — column
  actions (add right/left, move right/left, delete) on header cells, row actions (add above/below,
  move up/down, delete) on data cells. A click while a text selection is active never opens the
  menu, so dragging to select cell text isn't interrupted
- Mermaid diagrams: a ```mermaid code block renders as a live diagram in the WYSIWYG view; pasting
  Mermaid syntax through "insert HTML" is auto-detected and inserted as a mermaid code block
  instead. The library is lazy-loaded (no bundle cost if unused) and runs with
  securityLevel: "strict"
- Cursor between blocks: clicking the free area to the right of a table (or its margin, or the gap
  between two blocks) puts a gap cursor there instead of inside a cell/code block; Enter inserts a
  blank line at that point and typing writes there. A click above a table writes before it. When
  the document ends in a block (table, code block, Mermaid diagram, quote, list, rule, image) an
  empty paragraph always follows it, and a click to its right/below puts the cursor there. Helper
  lines never fire onChange on creation and are not serialized to Markdown; skipped in `onlyView`
- Cursor position is preserved (best effort) when toggling between the rendered and Markdown views
- Link UX: inserting a link with text already selected only asks for the URL (applies it to that
  exact text); URLs without a protocol get `http://` auto-prepended; clicking an existing link in
  the rendered view opens a popover (go to URL / copy URL / edit URL — with an inline remove-link
  option — or, in `onlyView`, just go-to and copy)
- `onlyView` prop (default false): read-only viewer mode, toolbar collapses to a notice + export
  button only; `onlyViewNotice` customizes that notice text (e.g. to show a file name)
- Imperative API via `ref` (`MarkdownEditorHandle`): `reset()` restores the content the editor was
  mounted with, `isModified()` reports whether the content differs from it — for discard-changes
  and unsaved-changes flows without remounting
- `documentId` / `fileName` props: passive identifiers the consuming app can attach to the editor
- `showToolbar` prop (default true): show/hide the toolbar (including the reduced `onlyView` bar) at runtime
  without losing content, caret, undo history or view mode; toggling never fires onChange
- Compare mode: `mode="compare"` plus optional `compareOrientation` (`"side-to-side"` default | `"up-and-down"`) and
  `compareContent` (new Markdown) shows the original (read-only) and the new content (editable) in two
  panes with changed/added words highlighted yellow (`<mark>`, themable with `--mdw-compare-highlight-bg`)
  in both the rendered and Markdown views. A second bar offers "Rechazar cambio", "Aceptar cambio" and
  "Restaurar" (only when the new pane differs from `compareContent`); accept/reject call `onChange` and
  `onCompareDecision({ decision: "accepted" | "rejected", markdown })` and the control returns to default
  mode. The original only changes when the user accepts: if the host leaves compare mode (or removes
  `compareContent`) without a decision, the editor returns to the original (`onChange` reports it if it differed);
  `compareContent=""` is a valid empty proposal. The bar follows `showToolbar`. `reset()` = Restaurar, `isModified()` = Restaurar visible
- Compare scroll sync: `compareSyncScroll` prop (default true). In `mode="compare"` scrolling either pane scrolls
  the other to the matching content (top edge of the scrolled pane; the pane scrolled last leads). Matching reuses
  the diff: paired blocks in the rendered view, identical lines in the Markdown view; passages present on one side
  only are crossed proportionally; with no common content it is proportional; top/bottom map to top/bottom.
  Vertical only, no animation; typing in the new pane never moves it. `false` = independent panes
- Version history: opt-in `historyUndo` prop (default false). A version of the Markdown is saved after 3 s
  without changes (max 200, in memory only). A clock icon right after the HTML button of the toolbar (default mode only)
  opens history mode: a bar with Undo / Redo / Confirm / Cancel (back to last version) under the toolbar and a right-hand list of
  versions with their time (click an entry to jump to that version); the document is read-only while browsing and `onChange` is not called. Confirm
  keeps the shown version (notifies once if it differs from the content at entry, appended as newest version);
  Cancel (back to last version) restores the content at entry. Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y act as Undo / Redo
  while open. Closes without applying on prop off, `onlyView`, compare mode or `showToolbar={false}`
- `resizable` prop (default true): native CSS `resize: both` drag handle, like a `<textarea>`; ignored with `autoHeight`
- `autoHeight` prop (default false): the control grows downward with its content so there is no inner vertical
  scrollbar (shrinks back when content is removed); `height` becomes the minimum, no resize handle; works in both views,
  compare mode (taller pane / both stacked), `onlyView` and history mode; horizontal scroll of wide content kept
- `allowContentZoom` prop (default false): Ctrl/Cmd + wheel over the content or Ctrl/Cmd + `+`/`-`/`0` zooms the
  content 50–300 % (10 % steps) without resizing the control or the toolbar; no on-screen controls; the level is written
  as `--mdw-content-zoom` on the root (host sets the starting value via CSS and can read it); never fires onChange
- `autoHideBar` prop (default false): the toolbar is shown only while focus is inside the component (menus, dialogs and
  popovers count as inside) and removed from layout and tab order when focus leaves; `showToolbar={false}` wins; the
  compare and history bars are not affected
- All props with defaults: `initialContent` (""; read at mount only), `onChange` (—), `width` (700), `height` (500;
  minimum with `autoHeight`), `sanitizeEmbeddedHtml` (true), `className` (—; theming entry point), `onlyView` (false),
  `resizable` (true), `autoHeight` (false), `showToolbar` (true), `autoHideBar` (false), `allowContentZoom` (false), `onlyViewNotice`
  ("Edición desactivada"), `mode` ("default"), `compareOrientation` ("side-to-side"), `compareContent` (—), `onCompareDecision` (—),
  `historyUndo` (false), `compareSyncScroll` (true), `documentId` (—), `fileName` (—), `resolveImageSrc` (—; mount time)
- Theming via CSS Custom Properties (no extra props): 52 `--mdw-*` variables (base colors, toolbar incl. `--mdw-toolbar-scale` (default 1), content incl. `--mdw-content-padding` (default `12px 16px`), `--mdw-content-wysiwyg-font-size` (14px), `--mdw-content-markdown-font-size` (13px) and `--mdw-content-zoom` (1),
  tables/code, syntax highlighting, quotes, controls, menus/dialogs/popovers, compare highlight, scrollbars). Declare
  them on the class passed in `className`, on any ancestor or on `:root` (priority: control class > nearest ancestor >
  built-in default); the component never declares the public variables (defaults are fallbacks of private `--_mdw-*`
  tokens), so they work in any stylesheet load order without `!important`. Floating menus/dialogs copy the values.
  Full list, recipes (dark theme, OS preference, brand color, fonts, flat toolbar, backgrounds) and troubleshooting:
  [How to style it in your host (Spanish)](https://github.com/ferkiernan/mdwysiwyg/blob/master/docs/THEMING.md)
- Embedded HTML sanitized by default (XSS-safe), opt-out via `sanitizeEmbeddedHtml={false}` for
  trusted content

## Quick usage

```bash
npm install mdwysiwyg
```

```tsx
import { MarkdownEditor } from "mdwysiwyg";
import "mdwysiwyg/styles.css";

<MarkdownEditor
  initialContent="# Hello\n\n**world**"
  onChange={(markdown) => save(markdown)}
/>
```

## Clone instead of install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ferkiernan/mdwysiwyg.git
cd mdwysiwyg
npm install
npm run dev   # demo playground at http://localhost:5173
```
